A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of the same work, Training-Free Exponential Context Extension via Cascading KV Cache. Comparison covers all text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices; pages 2–20 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v3 reports original latency, PG19 perplexity, Booksum, passkey retrieval, and LongBench experiments in Section 4, plus appendix results including MMLU and InfiniteBench.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including the MMLU and InfiniteBench evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1–3, and Appendix C.1 retain the same cascading cache, token selection, positional encoding, strided prefill, and MInference integration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same PG19, Booksum, LongBench, passkey retrieval, MMLU, and InfiniteBench coverage. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments, including Streaming LLM, Flash Attention 2, BigBird, SnapKV, H2O, and the appendix comparisons involving MInference and PyramidKV.

E3.justification: Cache budgets, model configurations, strides, PG19 book selection, prompt truncation, passkey generation and scoring, and appendix evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The token-selection, stride-size, cascade-count, and head-policy/reduction ablations are identical. Attention visualizations and supplementary PG19 analyses are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 passkey trials per insertion-range/sequence-length combination, totaling 600 retrievals. The reproducibility statement gives the same determinism-based explanation for omitting error bars; no statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match, including the appendix results. For example, Cascade's Llama 3.1 8B PG19 perplexity at a 16K cache remains 7.72 in Table 1, and its InfiniteBench mean remains 35.32 in Table 10.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the EMA and sparsity definitions, token-span reasoning, and appendix mathematical expressions are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free context extension, benchmark performance, and efficiency, including the 6.8-fold prefill latency comparison.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same sparsity/extrapolation tradeoff, degradation beyond eight cascades, and proposed future direction.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, model paths in Table 5, kernel pseudocode, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and appendix discussions retain the same citations and research positioning, including the relationships to MInference and PyramidKV.

P1.justification: On page 1, Sung Ju Hwang's email changes from sjhwang@kaist.ac.kr to sungju.hwang@kaist.ac.kr, and the arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 28 February 2025 to v4 dated 31 March 2025. All other wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18, Tables 1–10, algorithms, captions, and their placement are unchanged. The first-page email and version-stamp edits do not alter the document layout.

improvement.justification: The only differences are the author email and arXiv version/date stamp. The main text and appendices preserve all scientific content, evidence, explanations, and limitations, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
